nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: Ramipril 1.25 mg orally once daily (start); titrate up to 5 mg daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression; control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension (first‑line) and monitoring of creatinine/K⁺ after 1–2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile after 3 months and then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; CKD is a CV risk equivalent
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises statin therapy for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: Epoetin alfa 50 IU/kg subcutaneously three times weekly (adjust to maintain Hb 10–12 g/dL)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 10–12 g/dL achieved; then review every 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of chronic kidney disease (EPO deficiency)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ESA for CKD‑related anemia when Hb <10 g/dL and iron stores are adequate

contraindications.reason: eGFR 14 mL/min/1.73 m²; NSAIDs accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for pain, or non‑pharmacological pain management

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or a GLP‑1 receptor agonist with renal dose adjustment if glycaemic control needed

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; patient already receiving ACE‑I
contraindications.alternative: Use either ACE‑I or ARB alone (ACE‑I chosen here)
Avoid lithium; consider alternative mood stabiliser if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use non‑contrast imaging or apply prophylactic hydration and NAC if contrast unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure not provided – assumed elevated; will measure and titrate ramipril accordingly.
Serum potassium and baseline liver function tests not available – will obtain before initiating ramipril and atorvastatin.
Lipid profile not available – atorvastatin started as CKD is a CV risk equivalent per NG203.
Hemoglobin, ferritin and transferrin‑saturation not available – ESA initiation pending confirmation of anemia and iron repletion.
Patient weight not recorded – ESA dose will be calculated once weight is known.
Allergy status unknown – will verify no ACE‑I or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 1.25 mg daily (titrate to 5 mg) for proteinuric CKD and hypertension, initiate atorvastatin 20 mg daily for cardiovascular risk reduction, and begin epoetin alfa 50 IU/kg SC three times weekly to treat CKD‑related anemia once iron status is confirmed. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy, lithium, and unprotected IV contrast due to severe renal impairment. Monitor BP, serum K⁺, creatinine, liver enzymes, lipid profile, and hemoglobin per NICE NG203 recommendations, with regular follow‑up and annual medication review.
